app/Console/Commands/PurgeExports.php:70 the $expired parameter is untyped (it should be Builder)

app/Console/Commands/PurgeExports.php:79, database/factories/ExportFactory.php:22, tests/Feature/PurgeExportsTest.php:135 use inline FQCNs (\RuntimeException, \DateTimeInterface, \Illuminate\Filesystem\FilesystemAdapter) instead of imports
tests/Feature/PurgeExportsTest.php:135-146 swaps the disk with an anonymous FilesystemAdapter subclass. That is heavy compared with a mock

Uses ConfirmableTrait with --force. Dry-run runs before confirmation and doesn't take the lock, so support can preview in production
lazyById(500) plus an index on created_at, behind a reusable createdBefore #[Scope]

bugs: An exception from $export->delete() (a DB error or a model event) isn't caught (app/Console/Commands/PurgeExports.php:88). The probe showed it aborts the whole run with an uncaught exception, so the remaining exports aren't processed. That falls short of 'carry on with the rest'
Files that fail with a false return (no exception) are counted but never report()ed or logged with their path, so ops only see an aggregate number (PurgeExports.php:82-86)
Same fixed 3600s lock TTL as impl-1 (PurgeExports.php:43). A long run can lose the lock and overlap with a manual run
antipatterns: app/Console/Commands/PurgeExports.php:30 wraps the query in a closure factory ($exports = fn () => ...) where a plain builder would do, since lazyById clones the builder
app/Console/Commands/PurgeExports.php:42 has a comment that restates what the lock does
strengths: The purge loop is clean: lazyById over a createdBefore #[Scope], file deleted first, row kept on failure, counts returned
The lock is released in finally (verified after an exception), and the schedule uses onOneServer with --force

Tests mock the Filesystem contract for both a false return and a thrown exception, and cover lock release, the disk config, more than one chunk (1100 rows), invalid --days, dry-run in production, and the schedule expression
The production refusal is tested, but it relies on the prompt's default rather than asserting a confirmation (no test of the confirmed 'yes' path)

v.rationale:
I've ranked impl-1 first, by a narrow margin. The two implementations are almost the same: same model, scope, migration index, disk, ConfirmableTrait/--force, dry-run before confirmation, Cache::lock with finally, lazyById, and an onOneServer schedule. All tests pass in both (impl-2: 17, impl-1: 15).

The deciding difference is in how they handle errors. In impl-1, the try/catch covers the whole per-row operation, so a failing row delete is reported and skipped and the run carries on. In impl-2, only the file delete is protected. My probe confirmed that an exception from the row delete aborts the entire run, which goes against 'carry on with the rest'. impl-2 also never reports files that fail by returning false, so ops only get a count.

impl-1's tests also exercise the real interactive confirmation for both yes and no. impl-2's tests are a little broader on mocking (exception path, lock release, disk config) and its code is slightly leaner. impl-1 loses some points for using an exception as control flow, inline FQCNs, and a heavyweight anonymous adapter in a test.

Both share the same weakness: a fixed 1-hour lock TTL, which could let a manual run overlap the nightly one on a very long run.
